entries.title: Measuring yourself against drug-assisted physiques and programmes
entries.take: Anabolic drugs add muscle that training alone does not, so the size, rate of progress and training loads of enhanced athletes do not transfer to drug-free lifters.
entries.body: In controlled trials testosterone raised muscle size and strength without any training, and lean mass gain climbed with dose. In the 1995 FFMI study only steroid users went past an index of 25. Lyle McDonald adds points from coaching: users recover from more volume and frequency, hold muscle and hormones better while dieting, and progress on almost any programme, which is why he distrusts training and diet advice built on their results. He notes that drug-free bodybuilders are about the size they were decades ago while professionals have kept growing. The trials also record harm, such as falling HDL cholesterol.
do: Compare your progress with drug-free ranges and with your own past numbers.
Judge a programme by its results in drug-free lifters at your level.

mcdonald-body-composition-meaning.title: What Does Body Composition Mean?
mcdonald-body-composition-meaning.support: Backs the two-part model (fat mass plus fat-free mass) and the point that water lost early in a diet counts as fat-free mass.

mcdonald-ffmi-2.title: Another Look at FFMI: Part 2
mcdonald-ffmi-2.support: Backs the points that fat-free mass is not all muscle, that high body fat inflates FFMI and that exceptions above 25 are rare.

mcdonald-body-composition-calculations.title: Body Composition Calculations
mcdonald-body-composition-calculations.support: Backs the fat mass, lean mass and target-weight arithmetic and the point that fat loss moves the percentage more than equal muscle gain.

kouri-1995.title: Fat-Free Mass Index in Users and Nonusers of Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids
kouri-1995.support: We calculated FFMI in 157 male athletes, comprising 83 users of anabolic-androgenic steroids and 74 nonusers. The normalized FFMI values of athletes who had not used steroids extended up to a well-defined limit of 25.0; that of some users exceeded 30. 20 Mr. America winners (1939-1959) had a mean of 25.4.

heymsfield-2014.title: Weight loss composition is one-fourth fat-free mass: a critical review and critique of this widely cited rule
heymsfield-2014.support: A widely cited rule states that approximately one-fourth of weight loss will be FFM, with the remaining three-fourths being fat mass. Temporal effects are examined as are lean tissue moderating effects such as ageing, inactivity and exercise.

forbes-2000.title: Body Fat Content Influences the Body Composition Response to Nutrition and Exercise
forbes-2000.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
forbes-2000.support: In experiments of at least 3-weeks' duration, the weight gain of thin people comprises 60-70% lean tissues, whereas in the obese it is 30-40%. There is an inverse curvilinear relationship between initial body fat content and the proportion of weight loss consisting of lean tissue.

ackland-2012.title: Current Status of Body Composition Assessment in Sport
ackland-2012.support: To date, there is no universally applicable criterion or 'gold standard' methodology for body composition assessment. When profiling change in interventions, single methods whose raw data are surrogates for body composition (with the notable exception of the body mass index) remain useful.

van-marken-lichtenbelt-2004.title: Body Composition Changes in Bodybuilders: A Method Comparison
van-marken-lichtenbelt-2004.support: 27 male bodybuilders; the 4C model served as the gold standard. The descriptive methods (DXA, BMI equations, skinfolds, bioimpedance) had small biases (exception BMI) but relatively large errors (range: 5.5-8%).

mcdonald-measurement-problems.title: Problems with Measuring Body Composition
mcdonald-measurement-problems.support: Backs the density-assumption problem, skinfold equation limits and his position that consistent readings matter more than accurate ones.

friedl-1994.title: Lower limit of body fat in healthy active men
friedl-1994.support: 55 normal young men during an 8-wk Army course; percent body fat by DEXA averaged 14.3% and 5.8% at the beginning and end. Our results suggest that 4-6% BF or approximately 2.5 kg fat represents the lower limit for healthy men.

kyle-2004.title: Bioelectrical impedance analysis—part II: utilization in clinical practice
kyle-2004.support: BIA works well in healthy subjects and in patients with stable water and electrolytes balance with a validated BIA equation that is appropriate with regard to age, sex and race. Use in subjects at extremes of BMI ranges or with abnormal hydration cannot be recommended for routine assessment.

nana-2015.title: Methodology Review: Using Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) for the Assessment of Body Composition in Athletes and Active People
nana-2015.journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
nana-2015.support: Best practice protocol includes standardization of subject presentation (subjects rested, overnight-fasted and in minimal clothing) and positioning on the scanning bed.

ball-2004-men.title: Comparison of anthropometry to DXA: a new prediction equation for men
ball-2004-men.support: 160 men aged 18-62 y. Although %BF was significantly correlated (r=0.923-0.942) with DXA for all three equations, each equation underestimated %BF (range=3.1-3.3%) compared to DXA.

mcdonald-measuring-body-composition.title: Measuring Body Composition: Part 1
mcdonald-measuring-body-composition.support: Backs the survey of methods: what calipers, BIA, underwater weighing, DEXA, tape and photos each do well and badly.

ball-2004-women.title: Comparison of Anthropometry to Dual Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry: A New Prediction Equation for Women
ball-2004-women.journal: Research Quarterly for Exercise and Sport
ball-2004-women.support: The percentage of body fat by anthropometry was significantly correlated (r = .896-.929) with DXA, but each equation underestimated %BF (3.2-5.6 %BF) in a sample of 150 women.

mcdonald-dexa-vs-calipers.title: DEXA versus Calipers for Bodyfat
mcdonald-dexa-vs-calipers.support: Backs the point that DEXA reads higher than caliper-era figures and that numbers from different methods should not be compared.

jackson-1978.title: Generalized equations for predicting body density of men
jackson-1978.support: Skinfold thickness, body circumferences and body density were measured in samples of 308 and ninety-five adult men ranging in age from 18 to 61 years. The regression equations were shown to be valid for adult men varying in age and fatness.

dixon-2006.title: The effect of acute fluid consumption on measures of impedance and percent body fat using leg-to-leg bioelectrical impedance analysis
dixon-2006.support: 21 recreationally active men consumed 591 ml of water or a carbohydrate/electrolyte drink. A slight overestimation in %BF (approximately 0.5%) was observed due to increased body weight.

bone-2017.title: Manipulation of Muscle Creatine and Glycogen Changes Dual X-ray Absorptiometry Estimates of Body Composition
bone-2017.support: Eighteen well-trained male cyclists. Glycogen loading, both with and without creatine loading, resulted in substantial increases in estimates of lean body mass (3.0% and 2.0%). A substantial decrease in leg lean mass was observed after the glycogen depleting condition (-1.4%).

kreitzman-1992.title: Glycogen storage: illusions of easy weight loss, excessive weight regain, and distortions in estimates of body composition
kreitzman-1992.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
kreitzman-1992.support: Glycogen is stored in hydrated form (three to four parts water); changes in total body potassium in 11 subjects after 4 days on a very-low-calorie diet reflected glycogen mobilization.

mcdonald-body-composition-recommendation.title: Body Composition Recommendations
mcdonald-body-composition-recommendation.support: Backs the tracking routine: which tools to combine, fixed conditions, how often to measure and using gym strength as a check on muscle.

white-2011.title: Fluid Retention over the Menstrual Cycle: 1-Year Data from the Prospective Ovulation Cohort
white-2011.support: 765 menstrual cycles in 62 healthy women. Fluid retention scores peaked on the first day of menstrual flow, were lowest during the mid-follicular period, and gradually increased over the 11 days surrounding ovulation.

mcdonald-body-composition-numbers.title: Body Composition Numbers
mcdonald-body-composition-numbers.support: Backs his caliper-era figures for health, sport and appearance and his position that lower body fat is not better past a point.

santos-2014.title: Reference Values for Body Composition and Anthropometric Measurements in Athletes
santos-2014.support: Body weight and height were measured in 898 athletes (264 female, 634 male), and 481 athletes (142 female and 339 male) with DXA. A total of 21 different sports were represented. Table 5 gives mean whole-body fat % and FFMI by sport and sex.

mcdonald-why-change-composition.title: Why Do People Change Body Composition?
mcdonald-why-change-composition.support: Backs the point that the best body fat level for a sport is not the lowest one an athlete can reach.

karpe-2015.title: Biology of upper-body and lower-body adipose tissue—link to whole-body phenotypes
karpe-2015.support: The abdominal depots are characterized by rapid uptake of predominantly diet-derived fat and a high lipid turnover that is easily stimulated by adrenergic receptor activation. The lower-body fat stores have a reduced lipid turnover.

mcdonald-stubborn-fat.title: Why is Stubborn Fat Stubborn?
mcdonald-stubborn-fat.support: Backs the receptor, blood-flow and insulin explanation for why hip, thigh and lower abdominal fat is released slowly.

considine-1996.title: Serum Immunoreactive-Leptin Concentrations in Normal-Weight and Obese Humans
considine-1996.support: Mean serum leptin concentrations were 31.3 ng per milliliter in 139 obese subjects and 7.5 in 136 normal-weight subjects. There was a strong positive correlation between serum leptin concentrations and the percentage of body fat (r = 0.85).

mcdonald-what-is-body-fat.title: What is Body Fat?
mcdonald-what-is-body-fat.support: Backs the description of fat tissue as a compact energy store and hormone-releasing organ, and the caution about adding fat cells.

neeland-2019.title: Visceral and ectopic fat, atherosclerosis, and cardiometabolic disease: a position statement
neeland-2019.support: Visceral adipose tissue, accurately measured by CT or MRI, is an independent risk marker of cardiovascular and metabolic morbidity and mortality. Ectopic fat deposition, including hepatic and epicardial fat, might contribute to increased atherosclerosis and cardiometabolic risk.

mcdonald-how-we-get-fat.title: How We Get Fat
mcdonald-how-we-get-fat.support: Backs the explanation that fat is stored directly while surplus carbohydrate and protein are burned in place of fat.

spalding-2008.title: Dynamics of fat cell turnover in humans
spalding-2008.support: The number of fat cells stays constant in adulthood in lean and obese individuals, even after marked weight loss. Approximately 10% of fat cells are renewed annually at all adult ages and levels of body mass index.

tchoukalova-2010.title: Regional differences in cellular mechanisms of adipose tissue gain with overfeeding
tchoukalova-2010.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
tchoukalova-2010.support: 28 healthy, normal weight adults (15 men). Lower-body fat responded to overfeeding by fat-cell hyperplasia, with adipocyte number increasing by 2.6 x 10(9) cells; fat-cell number increases in certain depots in adults after only 8 wk of increased food intake.

acheson-1988.title: Glycogen storage capacity and de novo lipogenesis during massive carbohydrate overfeeding in man
acheson-1988.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
acheson-1988.support: Three men. Glycogen storage capacity in man is approximately 15 g/kg body weight and can accommodate a gain of approximately 500 g before net lipid synthesis contributes to increasing body fat mass.

hall-2007.title: What is the required energy deficit per unit weight loss?
hall-2007.support: The rule of thumb approximately matches the predicted energy density of lost weight in obese subjects with an initial body fat above 30 kg but overestimates the cumulative energy deficit required per unit weight loss for people with lower initial body fat.

horton-1995.title: Fat and carbohydrate overfeeding in humans: different effects on energy storage
horton-1995.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
horton-1995.support: Nine lean and seven obese men overfed 50% above energy requirements for 14 d each. Carbohydrate overfeeding resulted in 75-85% of excess energy being stored; fat overfeeding had minimal effects on fat oxidation, leading to storage of 90-95% of excess energy.

mcdonald-whooshes.title: Of Whooshes and Squishy Fat
mcdonald-whooshes.support: Backs the observation that scale loss can arrive in sudden steps and his unproven water-retention explanation for it.

tomiyama-2010.title: Low Calorie Dieting Increases Cortisol
tomiyama-2010.support: 121 female participants were assigned randomly to one of four dietary interventions for 3 weeks. Restricting calories (1200 kcal/day) increased the total output of cortisol.

mcdonald-calorie-partitioning.title: Calorie Partitioning: Part 1
mcdonald-calorie-partitioning.support: Backs the definition of partitioning, his list of what governs it and his account of leptin's fall during dieting.

hall-2007-forbes.title: Body fat and fat-free mass inter-relationships: Forbes's theory revisited
hall-2007-forbes.support: Forbes's equation quantifies the fat-free proportion of a weight change as a function of the initial body fat. The extended equation was re-expressed in terms of the P-ratio and compared favourably with data from human underfeeding and overfeeding experiments.

mcdonald-initial-body-fat.title: Initial Body Fat and Body Composition Changes
mcdonald-initial-body-fat.support: Backs his argument that dieted-down people do not partition like naturally lean people, and his body fat range for gaining phases.

dulloo-1997.title: Poststarvation hyperphagia and body fat overshooting in humans: a role for feedback signals from lean and fat tissues
dulloo-1997.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
dulloo-1997.support: Reanalysis of the 12 starved and refed men in the Minnesota Experiment: the total hyperphagic response is inversely correlated with the degree of fat recovery (r = -0.6) as well as with that of FFM recovery (r = -0.5); explains poststarvation overshoot in body fat.

helms-2014-protein.title: A Systematic Review of Dietary Protein During Caloric Restriction in Resistance Trained Lean Athletes: A Case for Higher Intakes
helms-2014-protein.journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
helms-2014-protein.support: Six studies; protein needs for energy-restricted resistance-trained athletes are likely 2.3-3.1 g/kg of FFM scaled upwards with severity of caloric restriction and leanness.

mcdonald-single-digit.title: Muscle Loss While Dieting to Single Digit Body Fat Levels
mcdonald-single-digit.support: Backs his explanation of why lean dieters lose more lean tissue and what protects it.

mcdonald-leptin.title: Bodyweight Regulation: Leptin Part 1
mcdonald-leptin.support: Backs his account of leptin as a starvation signal, its fast fall on a diet and his case for carbohydrate-based refeeds.

leibel-1995.title: Changes in Energy Expenditure Resulting from Altered Body Weight
leibel-1995.support: Maintenance of a body weight at a level 10 percent or more below the initial weight was associated with a mean (+/- SD) reduction in total energy expenditure of 6 +/- 3 kcal per kilogram of fat-free mass per day in the subjects who had never been obese (P < 0.001) and 8 +/- 5 kcal per kilogram per day in the obese subjects (P < 0.001). Resting energy expenditure and nonresting energy expenditure each decreased 3 to 4 kcal per kilogram of fat-free mass per day in both groups of subjects.

rosenbaum-2005.title: Low-dose leptin reverses skeletal muscle, autonomic, and neuroendocrine adaptations to maintenance of reduced weight
rosenbaum-2005.support: 10 inpatient subjects maintaining a 10% reduced weight. During leptin administration, energy expenditure, skeletal muscle work efficiency, sympathetic nervous system tone, and circulating concentrations of thyroxine and triiodothyronine returned to pre-weight-loss levels.

heymsfield-1999.title: Recombinant Leptin for Weight Loss in Obese and Lean Adults
heymsfield-1999.support: Fifty-four lean and 73 obese adults. Mean weight changes at 24 weeks ranged from -0.7 (5.4) kg for the 0.01 mg/kg dose to -7.1 (8.5) kg for the 0.30 mg/kg dose. Exogenous leptin appears to induce weight loss in some obese subjects.

mcdonald-set-points.title: Set Point Settling Points and Bodyweight Regulation Part 1
mcdonald-set-points.support: Backs his reading that weight defence is lopsided and that set point and settling point both operate.

hickey-1996.title: Gender Differences in Serum Leptin Levels in Humans
hickey-1996.support: Fasting serum leptin concentration was 6.9 ng/ml in males (N = 333) and 15.2 ng/ml in females (N = 63). Total fat mass did not differ between groups (males 20.5 kg; females 20.4 kg), suggesting that females have higher leptin levels per unit fat mass.

dirlewanger-2000.title: Effects of short-term carbohydrate or fat overfeeding on energy expenditure and plasma leptin concentrations in healthy female subjects
dirlewanger-2000.support: Ten healthy lean females. Carbohydrate overfeeding for 3 days increased plasma leptin concentrations by 28%, and 24 h EE by 7%. Fat overfeeding did not significantly change plasma leptin concentrations or energy expenditure.

welt-2004.title: Recombinant Human Leptin in Women with Hypothalamic Amenorrhea
welt-2004.support: Eight women with hypothalamic amenorrhea received recombinant leptin for up to three months; treatment increased mean LH levels and LH pulse frequency after two weeks. Three patients had an ovulatory menstrual cycle.

speakman-2011.title: Set points, settling points and some alternative models: theoretical options to understand how genes and environments combine to regulate body adiposity
speakman-2011.support: The set point model is consistent with many biological aspects of energy balance but does not explain the rise in body weight since the 1980s; the settling point model accommodates environmental characteristics but struggles with biological and genetic aspects.

maclean-2011.title: Biology's response to dieting: the impetus for weight regain
maclean-2011.journal: American Journal of Physiology-Regulatory, Integrative and Comparative Physiology
maclean-2011.support: We summarize the evidence of biology's role in the problem of weight regain; the biological adaptations to an energy-restricted diet in the overweight and obese are reviewed.

levine-1999.title: Role of Nonexercise Activity Thermogenesis in Resistance to Fat Gain in Humans
levine-1999.support: 16 nonobese volunteers overfed by 1000 kcal/day for 8 weeks; changes in NEAT accounted for the 10-fold differences in fat storage.

mcdonald-neat-fat-gain.title: Nonexercise Activity Thermogenesis and Fat Gain
mcdonald-neat-fat-gain.support: Backs the reading of the 1999 overfeeding study and the thrifty versus spendthrift idea.

weyer-2001.title: Changes in energy metabolism in response to 48 h of overfeeding and fasting in Caucasians and Pima Indians
weyer-2001.support: 14 male subjects; 48 h of overfeeding and fasting in a respiratory chamber. The changes in 24-EE in response to overfeeding and fasting were positively correlated (r=0.70).

heymsfield-2007.title: Why do obese patients not lose more weight when treated with low-calorie diets? A mechanistic perspective
heymsfield-2007.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
heymsfield-2007.support: Weight-stable reduced-obese patients had a TEE almost identical to never-obese subjects (weighted mean difference: 1.3%). Obese subjects participating in LCD programs have a weight loss less than half of that predicted.

mcdonald-obese-lose-less.title: Why Do Obese People not Lose More Weight on a Diets
mcdonald-obese-lose-less.support: Backs his critique that the review measured expenditure after dieting, not during it, and left out daily movement.

mcdonald-ffmi-1.title: Another Look at the Fat-Free Mass Index (FFMI)
mcdonald-ffmi-1.support: Backs the summary of the 1995 FFMI study and his position that 25 is a practical, not absolute, ceiling.

abe-2018.title: Skeletal muscle mass in human athletes: What is the upper limit?
abe-2018.support: Ninety-five large-sized male athletes and 48 recreationally active males. Ten of the athletes had more than 100 kg of FFM, including the largest who had 120.2 kg, while seven had more than 50 kg of SM, including the largest who had 59.3 kg.

kanehisa-1998.title: Body composition and isokinetic strength of professional Sumo wrestlers
kanehisa-1998.support: 23 professional Sumo wrestlers: body mass ranged between 77.0 and 150.0 kg, relative fat mass between 11.9 and 37.0%, and fat-free mass between 59.1 and 107.6 kg.

van-etten-1994.title: Effect of body build on weight-training-induced adaptations in body composition and muscular strength
van-etten-1994.support: From a sedentary male population (N = 77) two groups with either a slender (N = 10) or a solid (N = 11) body build were selected. Training induced a significant increase in FFM in the solid group (1.6 kg, 2.3%) in contrast with the slender group, which showed no significant change.

hull-2011.title: Fat-free mass index: changes and race/ethnic differences in adulthood
hull-2011.support: A multi-ethnic sample of 1339 healthy adults; FFMI was greatest in African American and the least in Asian participants. The estimated turning point where FFMI started to decline was in the mid 20s for male and mid 40s for female participants.

mcdonald-ffmi-3.title: Another Look at FFMI: Part 3
mcdonald-ffmi-3.support: Backs the point that starting lean mass shapes final FFMI and that the amount of muscle gained matters more than the index.

mcdonald-genetic-potential.title: What’s My Genetic Muscular Potential?
mcdonald-genetic-potential.support: Backs his yearly muscle-gain model, the agreement between four prediction models and the warning about chasing faster gains.

mcdonald-metabolic-rate.title: Metabolic Rate Overview
mcdonald-metabolic-rate.support: Backs the four-part breakdown of daily energy expenditure and the point that people of equal size differ in resting metabolism.

johnstone-2005.title: Factors influencing variation in basal metabolic rate include fat-free mass, fat mass, age, and circulating thyroxine but not sex, circulating leptin, or triiodothyronine
johnstone-2005.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
johnstone-2005.support: A cross-sectional study of 150 white adults. Of the between-subject variance in BMR, 63% was explained by FFM, 6% by FM, and 2% by age. The effects of sex and bone mineral content were not significant. Twenty-six percent of the variance remained unexplained.

wang-2010.title: Specific metabolic rates of major organs and tissues across adulthood: evaluation by mechanistic model of resting energy expenditure
wang-2010.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
wang-2010.support: Specific resting metabolic rates (kcal/kg/d) suggested by Elia: 200 for liver, 240 for brain, 440 for heart and kidneys, 13 for skeletal muscle, 4.5 for adipose tissue, and 12 for residual organs and tissues; evaluated in nonobese, healthy adults (n = 131).

mcclave-2001.title: Dissecting the energy needs of the body
mcclave-2001.journal: Current Opinion in Clinical Nutrition and Metabolic Care
mcclave-2001.support: The majority of the resting energy expenditure can be explained by the energy needs of a few highly metabolic organs, making up a small percentage of the body by weight.

mcdonald-energy-needs.title: Dissecting the Energy Needs of the Body - Research Review
mcdonald-energy-needs.support: Backs his use of per-kilo tissue energy values to show that added muscle raises resting expenditure only slightly.

mcdonald-delayed-fat-loss.title: The LTDFLE
mcdonald-delayed-fat-loss.support: Backs his description of continued leaning-out in the week after a long diet and his labelled guesses about its cause.

levitsky-2006.title: Monitoring weight daily blocks the freshman weight gain: a model for combating the epidemic of obesity
levitsky-2006.support: Female freshmen weighed themselves each morning and received feedback from the most recent 7 days of weights. The untreated controls gained 3.1 kg and 2.0 kg, whereas weight gain of the experimental groups was 0.1 kg and -0.82 kg, values not significantly different than zero.

mcdonald-bmi-weighing.title: Of BMI and Weighing Frequency
mcdonald-bmi-weighing.support: Backs the advice to weigh often, act on a rolling average and pair the scale with a second measure.

bhasin-1996.title: The Effects of Supraphysiologic Doses of Testosterone on Muscle Size and Strength in Normal Men
bhasin-1996.support: We randomly assigned 43 normal men to one of four groups. Among the no-exercise groups, those given testosterone had greater increases in bench-press (9 vs. -1 kg) and squatting strength (16 vs. 3 kg). The men assigned to testosterone and exercise had greater increases in fat-free mass (6.1 kg).

mcdonald-steroids-muscle.title: Anabolic Steroids and Muscle Growth
mcdonald-steroids-muscle.support: Backs the choice of controlled testosterone trials summarised here and his reading of what they mean for comparisons.

bhasin-2001.title: Testosterone dose-response relationships in healthy young men
bhasin-2001.journal: American Journal of Physiology-Endocrinology and Metabolism
bhasin-2001.support: 61 eugonadal men, 18-35 yr, were randomized to one of five groups for 20 wk. Fat-free mass increased dose dependently (change +3.4, 5.2, and 7.9 kg) and correlated with log testosterone concentrations (r = 0.73); changes in fat mass and plasma HDL cholesterol were negatively correlated.

sinha-hikim-2002.title: Testosterone-induced increase in muscle size in healthy young men is associated with muscle fiber hypertrophy
sinha-hikim-2002.journal: American Journal of Physiology-Endocrinology and Metabolism
sinha-hikim-2002.support: Muscle biopsies were obtained in 39 men before and after 20 wk. The increases in muscle volume are associated with concentration-dependent increases in cross-sectional areas of both type I and type II muscle fibers and myonuclear number.

bhasin-1997.title: Testosterone Replacement Increases Fat-Free Mass and Muscle Size in Hypogonadal Men 1
bhasin-1997.journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
bhasin-1997.support: Seven hypogonadal men, 19-47 yr of age, were treated for 10 weeks. Fat-free mass, measured by underwater weighing, increased from 56.0 to 60.9 kg (change, +5.0 kg), but percent fat did not significantly change.

mcdonald-drugs-help.title: Do Drugs Only Help a Little?
mcdonald-drugs-help.support: Backs his argument that drug-assisted size, recovery and training loads are not a fair yardstick for drug-free lifters.

harty-2019.title: Upper and lower thresholds of fat-free mass index in a large cohort of female collegiate athletes
harty-2019.support: 372 female collegiate athletes underwent body composition assessment via dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry. Average FFMI was 18.82±2.08 kg/m2. FFMI in rugby athletes was 20.09, cross country 16.56, Olympic weightlifting 19.69. The upper threshold for FFMI in female athletes (97.5th percentile) was 23.90 kg/m2.
